decision: read the PRD features (F1-F12) and HANDOFF before choosing what to build
why: the ask is to build what the PRD promises and the code lacks, so the gap list has to come from the documents and the code, not memory
result: candidate gaps noted; sent to independent audit

decision: workers use local Postgres, not Supabase
why: the DATABASE_URL in this sandbox points at production and its port 5432 refuses connections; the operator said to use local Postgres when Supabase is not reachable
result: each worker gets its own local database

decision: split the audit across five read-only auditors on Opus medium
why: a second read that did not start from my guesses; reading the whole codebase myself would crowd out the build work
evidence: pstack swarm skill; slices F1+F9, F2-F4, F5+F6+F8, F7+F10+F11, F12

decision: five auditors reported; the biggest finding is that rules D8, D9 and D10 can never fire on a real run
why: the pipeline never fills the three inputs those rules read, so notices and referrals only exist in unit tests
result: confirmed by reading respond(): the three fields are not set

decision: checked one auditor claim myself: officers cannot verify or reject a citizen report anywhere in the console
why: HANDOFF says verified reports feed the Dust Score, so a missing button would mean 15% of every score can never move
evidence: grep citizen_reports apps/web: one insert and two counts, no update
result: claim holds; added to the build list

decision: weather history for the local database comes from Open-Meteo's historical-forecast host, through a wrapper kept outside the repo
why: the archive host answers 429 'daily limit exceeded' from this sandbox today; the other host serves the same variables

decision: left out of the build: relay actuation, WhatsApp sending, BEST-bus nodes, MahaRERA scrape, SAFAR baseline, LLM explainer, permits
why: each needs hardware, a paid key, a private feed or a host this sandbox cannot reach
evidence: auditor reports (OUT rows); curl maharera -> no connection
result: will be filed as issues, not built

decision: grouped the gaps into 12 features in four waves; first wave is the forecast spec (#55), agent rules D8-D10 (#56) and citizen photo reports (#57)
why: first wave holds the gaps the PRD marks P0 that touch mostly different files, so three can be built at once and merged one after another

decision: arena with two candidates per feature on Opus xhigh, a judge and a verifier on Opus medium
why: the operator named these models; pstack arena wants the judge from another model family, which the operator's choice overrides
evidence: operator message of 23 Nov; pstack arena/SKILL.md Phase C
result: family check not run, by instruction

decision: each candidate has its own worktree, branch, two databases and port; only I push, through the one session branch
why: candidates on the same feature would otherwise overwrite each other, and the session may only push to claude/compassionate-thompson-khty9q

decision: builders start before the real-data database is ready and wait for it only when they need it
why: the load takes about 40 minutes because the OpenStreetMap mirrors time out first; tests and code do not need it

decision: started the second wave at the same time as the first: sensor audit (#58), exposure avoided (#59), public Dust Score (#60)
why: load average was 0.1 with six builders running, since they mostly wait on the model; web builds take turns behind one lock to protect memory
evidence: uptime at 12:36 UTC; RULES.md flock rule; issues 58, 59, 60

decision: public Dust Score (#60) has one builder and a verifier, not an arena
why: its shape is mostly fixed by the PRD and the existing public API, so a second candidate would mostly repeat the first

decision: moved the officer app behind citizen photo reports
why: both need a photo shrunk in the browser and stored in Postgres; building them at once would make two copies of the same plumbing
result: officer app waits for #57 to merge

decision: made every Python process single-threaded (OMP_NUM_THREADS=1) through a .pth file and stopped the starved test runs
why: eleven builders each ran LightGBM with one OpenMP thread per core; load hit 47 on 4 cores and one K-East run took 9.7 minutes

decision: all eleven builders stopped at the account's 5-hour usage limit; saved each worktree's unsaved changes as a wip commit
why: the session restarted and anything not committed in a worktree could be lost
evidence: worktrees forecast-c1, forecast-c2, audit-spec-c1, citizen-photo-c1 got wip commits
result: every candidate's work is in git

decision: K-East real-data load finished (83,623 measured CPCB hours, run on real weather); P-North reloading after the restart
why: the background load hit its time limit during the P-North step
